title: Choosing Before Acting: Comparative Value Estimation for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agents
description:
arXiv:2610.02330v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) rely on long-horizon tool invocation sequences for complex tasks, where each invocation can alter the task state and condition subsequent decisions. In long-horizon tool use, final-outcome rewards provide weak credit assignment over long interaction traces.
